intent: This join finds the hospital visit that the anaesthetic took place in.
This join finds the theatre case that the anaesthetic was given for.
This join finds the hospital visit that the theatre case belongs to.
This join finds the staff who are recorded against the anaesthetic, so that the first of them can be named as its provider.
This join finds the member of staff behind each entry in the anaesthetic's staff list.
This join finds the anaesthetic that an observation sheet was charted for.
This join finds the observation sheet that holds each reading.
This join finds the hospital visit that an observation sheet was charted in.
This join finds the anaesthetic that each recorded event belongs to.
This join finds the anaesthetic during which each dose or infusion was given.
This join finds the anaesthetic during which each airway device or line was placed.
This join finds the hospital visit in which each dose was given.
This join finds the definition of the medicine behind each dose, which carries its name.
This join finds the patient whom each hospital visit belongs to.
This join finds the patient whom each theatre case belongs to.
This join finds the further details that the second patient table holds for each patient, such as the date of death.
This join finds the ward that each hospital visit is recorded against.
This join finds the theatre case in which each operation was carried out.
This join finds the definition of each operation, which carries its name and code.
This join finds the hospital visit that each diagnosis was recorded in.
This join finds the definition of each diagnosis, which carries its code.
This filter keeps only the anaesthetics that have a start and whose stop, where one is recorded, is not before the start.
This filter leaves out the readings that the anaesthetist did not accept.
This filter keeps only the readings that have a time.
This filter keeps only the airway devices and lines that have a time of placement.
This filter leaves out the test patients that the hospital keeps for training and testing.
This filter keeps only the hospital visits that have a time of admission.
These mapping rows give each type of anaesthetic, such as general or regional, its standard concept.
These mapping rows mark the observation types that hold a charted blood pressure, whose systolic part becomes a measurement.
These mapping rows mark the observation types that hold a charted blood pressure, whose diastolic part becomes a measurement.
These mapping rows give each kind of airway device or line its standard concept.
These mapping rows give each value of the patient's recorded sex its standard concept.
This mapping row gives the time spent under anaesthesia a visit concept, where the vocabulary offers one.

These mapping rows hold two settings: the margin, in minutes either side of an anaesthetic, within which a reading or an event points at the anaesthetic, and whether the conversion writes a mean pressure calculated from each charted pressure.
